register.level: drowsy, mild, nursery-storyteller register with a touchy streak
register.summary: Speaks half-asleep: slow, agreeable murmurs ('Of course, of course'), a meandering bedtime story about three sisters in a treacle-well that drifts by sound association, and sudden prickly dignity when interrupted or crowded ('If you can't be civil…', 'not in that ridiculous fashion').

examples.text: Once upon a time there were three little sisters, and their names were Elsie, Lacie, and Tillie; and they lived at the bottom of a well—
Of course, of course; just what I was going to remark myself.
Yes, but I grow at a reasonable pace, not in that ridiculous fashion.

catchphrases.text: Of course, of course / Of course they were
Once upon a time there were three little sisters

sentence_style.length: mid-length (mean 11.5 words) drowsy clauses joined by 'and', trailing off with dashes; one-word murmurs between

patterns.rule: Bedtime-story narration that drifts by sound association (well / well in; things beginning with M: mouse-traps, moon, memory, muchness).

examples.text: They were learning to draw, and they drew all manner of things—everything that begins with an M—
—that begins with an M, such as mouse-traps, and the moon, and memory, and muchness—

patterns.rule: Sleepy one-word or stock replies, especially 'Treacle,' and dates in court.
Injured dignity: denies having slept, demands civility, objects to being crowded.

examples.text: I wasn't asleep, I heard every word you fellows were saying.
If you can't be civil, you'd better finish the story for yourself.
You've no right to grow here,

patterns.rule: Sleep-talk inversions that copy the tea-party's word-game in his own sleepy terms.

examples.text: You might just as well say, that 'I breathe when I sleep' is the same thing as 'I sleep when I breathe'!
One, indeed! And so these three little sisters—they were learning to draw, you know—

address.to_alice: you (bare); 'you' with a rebuke when crowded

examples.text: I wasn't asleep, I heard every word you fellows were saying.

forbidden_words.reason: he never hurries, orders or panics; urgency belongs to the White Rabbit and command to the Queen and King
his grievances are mild and self-regarding (civility, elbow-room); insults are the Hatter's and the Queen's

drift.change: Tea-party: drifting in and out of sleep; the storyteller whose tale meanders, touchy when interrupted.
Court: seated beside a growing Alice, the drowsiness gives way to prim complaint about being squeezed ('ridiculous fashion'), before he murmurs 'Treacle' again and is hustled out.

recitation_repertoire.note: His sleep-sung 'Twinkle, twinkle, twinkle, twinkle—' (ch007-d0056) is sung text, excluded from the hit-rate denominator.
